entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. Learned counsel for the petitioner and respondent No.2 in unison submit that the parties to the lis have arrived at settlement among themselves and file an application under Section 320(2) of the Cr.P.C. along with the affidavits of both the parties to that effect before this Court.

The application filed under Section 320 (2) of the Cr.P.C., reads as follows:
"2. There were certain differences with regard to trivial matters between petitioner and respondent No.2 and there were financial exchanges among them and due to the same the complaint was lodged by the complainant.
3. The advice of elders and well-wishers resulted in peace and tranquility and all the differences between the petitioner and Respondent NO.2 were amicably settled and petitioner on this day is returning the amount received from the respondent No.2 i.e.,
Rs.1,00,711/-.
The complainant and respondent No.2 have also filed affidavits to that effect.

sentences.text: The offence punishable under section 419 of IPC and 420 of IPC is compoundable offence with Permission of Hon'ble Court and hence the petitioner and the Respondent may be permitted compound the offences.
There is no legal impediment for this Hon'ble Court to accord permission as prayed for."

Though the offences alleged against the petitioner in the case at hand inter alia is one punishable under Section 420 of the IPC, I deem it appropriate to accept the application filed under Section 320 of the Cr.P.C. and terminate the proceedings against the petitioner as the allegations are not against the State.

For the aforesaid reasons, I pass the following:
ORDER (i) The criminal petition is disposed.
(ii) The investigation / proceedings Crime No.134/2023, pending before the VII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru, stand quashed.
